the liver acts as a reservoir for protective CD8+ T-cells and the spleen as a source compartment for these cells, and that the spleen and liver have opposing effects on the generation of protective CD8+ liver resident T-cells during priming and boosters.

the development of efficient immunization protocols against Plasmodium infection and aims to understand the underlying mechanisms of CD8+ T-cell dynamics
the analysis of the dynamics of CD8+ T-cell responses to Plasmodium sporozoites in different organs of the immune system.
the development of a mathematical model of the dynamics of the CD8+ T lymphocyte response to Plasmodium infection.

, in the context of malaria, the spleen is the main source compartment for the generation of liver-residents CD8+ T effector cells during priming.
, the spleen is the primary source of CD8+ T-cells that migrate to the liver and become memory cells.

the spleen and liver play a critical role in the development of protective immunity against P.berghei sporozoite infection, and that the interplay between these organs and their T cell populations is essential to the formation of long-lasting memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spleen is the major source of hepatic CD8+ memory cells and their generation is dependent on the frequency of booster injections.
we have identified that the spleen is the critical source of CD8+ T-cells for priming, and that the liver is critical for the generation of memory T-cells.
the liver acts as a reservoir of memory CD8+ T-cells that is refilled upon subsequent booster injections, while the spleen acts mainly during priming as a source compartment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spleen and liver act as critical sources and sinks of protective CD8+ T lymphocytes during the priming and boosting phases of vaccination, respectively.
the spleen is the critical source compartment during the priming phase, whereas the liver is the main source compartment during booster injections.

the spleen and liver act in a complementary manner to induce protective liver-resident memory T cells, and that this is especially true during the first vaccination, when the spleen is the primary source of liver-resident T cells.
